claim: Three commits in effect@4.0.0-rc.115..a7a71921de touch packages/effect/src/unstable/ai or unstable/rpc: a2c4154cf8 (#7265 v2026-07-28 adapter), 49e4b37b83 (#8228 strictness/instructions/titles), 553c403f1d (#8235 RpcClient only). #8242 (769f6046a2) rewrites MCP migration YAML only.
McpServer named-export set is unchanged (15 symbols). run/layer/layerStdio/layerHttp gain optional instructions?: string. path and allowedOrigins remain on layerHttp.

registerToolkit/toolkit/registerResource/resource/registerPrompt/prompt now Exclude McpRequestContext from handler requirements. toolkit() is still Layer.effectDiscard(registerToolkit) provided with McpServer.layer; it does not type as supplying McpRequestContext.
Upstream typetest requires that a resource handler which uses McpServerClient.useSync still has Layer.Services = McpServerClient — registration no longer pretends the legacy client is in scope.

McpRequestContext is a new protocol-neutral Context.Service (clientId, protocolVersion: string, clientCapabilities, optional clientInfo/requestMetadata/inputResponses/requestState) with no getClient and no initializePayload. clientCapabilities now requires it.
McpServerClient.protocolVersion is StatefulProtocolVersion; optional requestMetadata was added. initializePayload, clientInfo, and getClient remain.
McpServer.elicit still requires McpServerClient and still yield*s getClient.

RPC middleware that provides McpServerClient Effect.dies when selectedProtocol.protocolVersion === "2026-07-28". provideInvocationContext attaches McpServerClient only when invocation.serverClient is defined.

G4 (v2026_07_28-only protocols list) is type-legal because v2026_07_28 is a ProtocolAdapter, but stdio initialize frames still call selectStatefulProtocol. A v2026-only server compiles and then does not treat initialize as a stateful handshake. This challenges G4 as a drop-in flip.
The McpServer public service no longer exposes initializedClients. Registration handlers on addTool/addResource/addPrompt require McpRequestContext; callTool still requires McpServerClient.

McpProtocol.ProtocolVersion includes "2026-07-28"; StatefulProtocolVersion excludes it. AnyProtocolAdapter carries runtime: RuntimeDescriptor instead of a transport field. v2026_07_28 is ProtocolAdapter<"2026-07-28", StatelessRuntimeDescriptor>; historical adapters are StatefulRuntimeDescriptor.

Tool input JSON Schema is exported as ToolJson (object-rooted). ToolOutputJson is new and allows any JSON Schema root. McpSchema.Tool.outputSchema is optional(ToolOutputJson). There is no ToolJsonSchema export.

Elicitation form schemas are named ElicitationString/ElicitationNumber/ElicitationBoolean, Untitled/Titled Single/Multi SelectEnum, LegacyTitledEnum, and ElicitationEnum. The *Schema names (StringSchema, EnumSchema, ToolJsonSchema, etc.) are not exported.

New McpSchema symbols include HEADER_MISMATCH_ERROR_CODE (-32020, not a member of the McpError union), InputRequired, McpInputRequest, and McpInputResponse. InputRequired's constructor requires inputRequests or requestState.
Toolkit.handle has an optional 4th argument options?: SchemaAST.ParseOptions. MCP registerToolkit passes { onExcessProperty: "error" } when Tool.getStrictMode(tool) === true.

Tool.FailureOrigin and Toolkit.FailureOrigin exist ("parameters" | "handler" | "result"). HandlerResult has optional failureOrigin. MCP registerToolkit maps parameters+ToolParameterValidationError to InvalidParams and handler+declared failure to isError:true without structuredContent.

Tool.Strict JSDoc describes provider structured-output. MCP reuses Tool.getStrictMode(tool) === true for excess-property rejection and Effect.dies at registration for strict raw JSON Schema dynamic tools before any tool in that toolkit is added.
Default Tool.Strict (undefined) is closed for OpenAI (getStrictMode ?? config.strictJsonSchema ?? true) but open for MCP (=== true is false). The two consumers diverge on the default.
registerPrompt/prompt accept optional title?: string and forward it onto McpSchema.Prompt. The Prompt schema already has a title field.
addTool handler success type includes InputRequired alongside CallToolResult. addPrompt success includes InputRequired alongside GetPromptResult. callTool still requires McpServerClient.

RpcServer.layerProtocolStdio and RpcSerialization.jsonRpc public signatures are unchanged. jsonRpc decodes JSON-RPC error objects as Cause Fail/error (not Die/defect). MCP wraps jsonRpc in mcpJsonRpcSerialization.

McpServer.tst.ts covers McpRequestContext, v2026_07_28/StatelessRuntimeDescriptor, ToolJson vs scalar ToolOutputJson, InputRequired constructability, and resource-still-requires-McpServerClient. It does not type-test instructions, prompt title, Toolkit.handle ParseOptions, FailureOrigin, or a v2026-only protocols list.
Tool.tst.ts covers FailureResult/ExecutionFailure and Tool.make defaults only. It does not mention FailureOrigin, HandlerResult.failureOrigin, or Tool.Strict.

Changeset modern-mice-discover.md only says protocol 2026-07-28 was added. It does not mention McpRequestContext, ToolJson, elicitation renames, InputRequired, HEADER_MISMATCH_ERROR_CODE, or AnyProtocolAdapter.runtime.

McpServer.yaml toolkit note claims the registration layer supplies McpRequestContext instead of excluding McpServerClient. Code of toolkit() excludes McpRequestContext and does not provide it; request-time supply is provideInvocationContext/middleware. The resource typetest is the counterexample.

McpSchema.yaml McpServerClient note matches code: use McpRequestContext for protocol-neutral handlers; McpServerClient is not provided by the 2026-07-28 adapter; registration helpers exclude McpRequestContext, not McpServerClient.
Tool.yaml and Toolkit.yaml do not mention FailureOrigin, HandlerResult.failureOrigin, Toolkit.handle ParseOptions, or MCP reuse of Tool.Strict.

strict-mcp-tool-inputs changeset says invalid arguments use InvalidParams on protocols before 2025-11-25 and isError:true on newer. registerToolkit handleCause always Effect.fail(new InvalidParams(...)). Tests observe INVALID_PARAMS_ERROR_CODE for strict excess properties. Protocol re-projection is unverified in this lane.

McpServer.yaml McpServer note says initializedClients and notificationsMailbox are no longer exposed. The current public service has neither field. notificationsMailbox is not a current (nor, in this lane's rc.115 read, prior) public-service field — the mailbox clause is a v3 leftover.

beep-effect in-repo servers still pass protocols: [McpProtocol.v2025_06_18] (nlp, m365, uspto, gov-legal, practice-kg layerStdio; professional-desktop layerHttp with allowedOrigins). Constructor option types remain compatible with HEAD minus the protocol value flip.

mcp-kit sanitizedToolkit still Exclude<HandlerServices, McpServerClient> and still yield*s serviceOption(McpServerClient) in addTool handle, while upstream toolkit now excludes McpRequestContext. Kit stubs construct McpServerClient with protocolVersion "2025-06-18" (still a StatefulProtocolVersion).

McpServer.layer (static) is typed Layer<McpServer | McpServerClient> via as any while implementation only builds McpServer. beep-effect kit fixtures already document that callTool dies without a stub.
elicit remaining on McpServerClient plus middleware die on 2026-07-28 means a G4-only in-repo server cannot use reverse-client elicitation.

McpError is a union of ParseError, InvalidRequest, MethodNotFound, InvalidParams, InternalError, and McpErrorBase, plus a typeof McpError.Type alias. HEADER_MISMATCH_ERROR_CODE is a constant, not a tagged union member.
McpServer.yaml constructor notes for layer/layerStdio/layerHttp/run still example only v2025_06_18 and do not mention instructions or v2026_07_28.
